name: Disambiguation Canvas
summary: A phone's orientation aims a sphere or cone at the target area; touching the screen lays all the objects caught out on a flat canvas mapped one-to-one to the touchscreen, and sliding the thumb onto the target and lifting selects it in one step.
howItWorks: In an HMD with an iPhone or iPod Touch, the device orientation points a 12° sphere or cone. On touch, the pre-selected objects animate (250 ms) into a grid on a rectangle parallel to the image plane, laid out within the thumb's comfortable reach (with a calibration of each user's reach); an arrow follows the thumb, and lifting off over an object selects it, or over empty space cancels. Against orientation-based raycasting (6 participants) it was slightly slower overall (2.37 s vs 2.29 s) but far more accurate and faster for the smallest targets; against SQUAD (11 participants) it was faster at every density, with hundreds of candidates handled in one step.
